raw.assessment: The incumbent honored all designs, but median work was 37 minutes. Rework clustered in large covers (5/8), versus medium (2/14) and small (0/18), supporting investigation of size-dependent fit without establishing a cause. Unadjusted small covers took 25–31 minutes; this does not establish attainable batch time. The concrete limiting observation is H2-O3: two customer failures involved rounded corners absent from reference tables, so passing the reference check cannot establish customer fit. Variable measured length shrinkage and missing width data further limit diagnosis. The reported 6.5% waste is a weight-based estimate, not verified area compliance.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may produce size-dependent dimensional errors; sewing and checking initial covers before cutting the remainder could expose a repeatable error early.
openings.delta: Changes feedback timing and tests the allowance instead of repeatedly correcting completed covers.
openings.prediction: If allowance error dominates, larger covers will show consistent signed fit errors associated with planned versus finished dimensions. Errors tracking operator, design, or cutting direction instead would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Stage initial ordered covers across the three sizes; record planned, cut, and finished dimensions, signed fit errors, operator, design, direction, and stage times. Measure retained samples in both axes through the stipulated wash test. Revise remaining cuts only if measurements and an area-based layout support the revision within existing stock, 8% waste, budget, and deadline.
assumptions: Initial covers remain usable ordered units.
A repeatable dimensional error can be distinguished from process variation; time savings remain unproven.

openings.claim: Does actual tabletop geometry explain customer installation failure after reference-table acceptance?
openings.delta: Tests whether the acceptance surface represents the customer's table.
openings.prediction: Similar-dimension tables with different corner radii would distinguish a corner mismatch from nominal-dimension error; failures increasing with measured dimension discrepancy would favor the latter.
openings.probe: Obtain dimensions and corner measurements from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare reference fit with observed first placement on their actual tables. Record discrepancies before proposing reversible pocket changes. Any changed construction must retain the ordered size/design and pass five wash cycles; assess the complete batch against 38/40 first fits and median work at most 32 minutes.
assumptions: Available tables provide informative geometry variation; six observations cannot establish batch success.

raw.assessment: A cover that locates itself on different corner profiles is conceivable, but neither its durability nor batch feasibility is established. The supplied failures motivate testing corner accommodation without assuming it explains the large-cover rework.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: corner pockets with short, concealed elastic gathering could seat the printed cover against the tabletop while accommodating modest corner-radius differences without repeated adjustment.
openings.delta: Replace fixed corner capture with compliant capture. Dependencies are sufficient panel dimensions, balanced tension, washable elastic and seams, unobstructed table undersides, and preserved visible design. Presently testable partial capability: determine whether a gathered offcut corner can seat consistently on square and rounded corners.
openings.prediction: With panel dimensions held constant, compliant pockets would reduce placement failures on rounded corners relative to fixed pockets, without introducing puckering or square-corner failures.
openings.probe: Use retained offcuts for paired corner mockups and seek a rounded-table trial from the six willing customers. Compare repeated placements with fixed pockets, then repeat after the stipulated wash test. Before stock cutting, cost materials and labor, verify the three-week schedule, and calculate cutting waste by area; advance only within 350 units and 8% waste.
assumptions: Suitable elastic is affordable and obtainable.
Corner capture contributes to the observed installation failures.
Required compliance does not distort the ordered design.

openings.claim: Do large-cover failures originate in panel size before corner capture, making compliant pockets insufficient?
openings.delta: Distinguish a whole-panel dimension deficit from a localized corner-seating problem.
openings.prediction: A panel deficit produces tension or shortfall across straight edges even with corners temporarily released; a corner-capture problem improves when only the pockets are released.
openings.probe: On the first medium and large covers, use temporary corner stitching and record straight-edge fit before and after releasing the pockets. Record actual tabletop dimensions, cutting direction and operator; include this trial labor in batch timing.
assumptions: Temporary stitching can be removed without damaging the purchased cloth.

openings.claim: Common allowance may cause size-dependent errors; staged sewing could prevent repeated rework.
openings.discriminator: Consistent signed dimensional errors versus operator/design/direction effects.
openings.probe: Stage usable covers across sizes; record planned/cut/finished dimensions, signed errors, operator/design/direction and stage times; wash offcuts measuring both axes before revising cuts.
openings.uncertainty: Repeatability and time savings unproven; width shrinkage unknown.

openings.claim: Reference tables may miss customer geometry failures.
openings.discriminator: Different radii at similar dimensions versus nominal-to-actual discrepancies.
openings.probe: Get six customers' dimensions/corners, prioritizing nominal-only orders; compare reference acceptance with actual first placement before reversible pocket changes.
openings.uncertainty: Measurement accuracy and geometry variation unknown; six trials cannot establish batch success.

openings.claim: Concealed elastic gathering might accommodate corner radii.
openings.discriminator: Equal panels: fewer rounded-corner failures without puckering or square-corner failures.
openings.probe: Compare fixed/gathered offcut pockets on square and customer rounded tables through repeated placements before/after five washes; cost labor/materials and check schedule/layout before cutting.
openings.uncertainty: Requires adequate panels, balanced tension, washable elastic/seams, clear undersides and undistorted design; availability and durability unproven.

openings.claim: Whole-panel deficits may make compliant pockets insufficient.
openings.discriminator: Straight-edge shortfall persists with pockets released versus improvement from release alone.
openings.probe: Temporarily stitch first medium/large corners; compare fit before/after release, recording actual table dimensions, direction, operator and trial labor.
openings.uncertainty: Stitch removal must avoid cloth damage.

post_distill.decision: Probe before commitment. Honor ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, tool-free removal and five washes; retain two machines, <=350 units, three weeks, <=8% area waste (6.5% weight estimate insufficient). Require >=38/40 first placements and median total labor <=32 minutes; no supplied evidence establishes these outcomes.
